scenario: AITA for going back on a promise I made to my wife post-affair? | First of all I’m aware I’m TA for cheating. That’s not what this post is about. When I owned up to my affair, my wife said she would stay with me if I agreed to make the next year “all about her.” I agreed because I thought this meant massages, shopping, doing her favorite things, etc. My wife decided to make this year all about Disney. She has never been obsessed with Disney stuff (our daughters loved Disney when they were little, but they’re out of the house now.) I suppose my wife always enjoyed Disney stuff but I assumed it was mostly for their sake. She has made me go to Disneyland 7 times this year and Harry Potter world once (which was actually nice, but the prices add up.) she had made me cosplay as Disney characters including a Beauty and the Beast costume that cost $800. She makes me watch Frozen every day and when I asked for a change she put on Pocahontas 2. I know this is nothing compared to her pain of being cheated on, but I’m miserable and can’t do it. I want to have an intervention where we stop all the Disney stuff and just go to counseling which should have happened a while ago. AITA for wanting to back out?

This can help individuals to stay grounded and focused on what is important to them. 3. **Reflection and introspection**: Regularly consulting a guiding text can encourage reflection and introspection, helping individuals to examine their thoughts, feelings, and actions. This self-reflection can lead to greater self-awareness, personal growth, and a deeper understanding of what is right and wrong. 4. **Accountability and responsibility**: Having a guiding text can also foster a sense of accountability and responsibility, as individuals may feel more inclined to consider the potential consequences of their actions and strive to make choices that align with their values and principles. 5. **Cultivating wisdom and discernment**: Regularly engaging with a guiding text can help individuals develop wisdom and discernment, enabling them to better navigate complex situations and make more informed decisions. In your case, returning to the Quran and Hadith when facing difficulties can provide a sense of comfort, guidance, and direction. It's as if you have a trusted advisor or mentor that offers valuable insights and principles to consider, helping you to make decisions that align with your values and faith. It's wonderful that you have this practice, and it's likely that it has a positive impact on your decision-making and overall well-being.
